note: Three axes: technical domain x role function x organizational context. Job titles are aliases for combinations, and none of the axes produces a ranking. This file is where changes are made. The eight axes, two scales and four levels use the same values as the Mechanical Engineering Core: results from two majors can only be compared on the same ruler, and building a new ruler for each major would break comparison within a university

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Did you turn the requirements into numbers and constraints?

J3.name: Technical decisions
J3.question: Which items did you decide yourself?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how?

J6.name: Comparison and verification
J6.question: What did you compare it against?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How did you narrow down what went wrong?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. The four axes asked at BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you were placed in one, and someone who has only done classes and a capstone will have that cell empty even if they made decisions. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth stage

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not use S8 as the denominator for S4. What the in-depth stage newly opens are the four axes not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use)

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.name: Literature and Source Research
technical_domains.owns: Decides the range to search and the materials to use

technical_domains.name: Text Analysis and Interpretation
technical_domains.owns: Decides the reading framework and the range of evidence

technical_domains.name: Language Structure Analysis
technical_domains.owns: Decides which units to divide language into for description

technical_domains.name: Corpus and Language Data
technical_domains.owns: Decides the data to collect and the annotation criteria

technical_domains.name: Translation and Interpreting
technical_domains.owns: Decides the unit of translation and what to keep
subareas: What to keep and what to drop

technical_domains.name: Writing and Editing
technical_domains.owns: Decides the range to revise with the readers in mind

technical_domains.name: Korean Language Education Design
technical_domains.owns: Decides the learners' level, the goals and the range to cover

technical_domains.name: Class Management and Assessment
technical_domains.owns: Decides the criteria for running classes and judging how much learning happened

technical_domains.name: Creative Writing and Structure
technical_domains.owns: Decides what to write and what structure to build

subareas: Words that work and words that do not

role_functions.name: Planning and Design
role_functions.success: One design where the range and order are written down and other people can use it as it is

role_functions.name: Analysis and Interpretation
role_functions.one_line: Reads the materials before reaching a conclusion
role_functions.output_kind: Analysis report · Text interpretation · Language description
role_functions.success: An interpretation whose evidence is in the materials and that changed a decision

role_functions.name: Review and Assessment
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether what was done is right
role_functions.output_kind: Review comments · Assessment rubric · Grading results
role_functions.success: A result where the judgment matches the criteria and the reviewed range is written down

role_functions.name: Production and Editing
role_functions.one_line: Edits the decided manuscript so that it comes out in the same form
role_functions.success: The same guidelines give the same quality, and it can be reversed

role_functions.name: Operations and Management
role_functions.one_line: Keeps courses and classes running properly
role_functions.output_kind: Operations log · Enrollment management · Course report
role_functions.success: Few interruptions, and records of recovery remain

role_functions.name: Integration and coordination
role_functions.one_line: Ties many people's decisions into one
role_functions.output_kind: Project plan · Schedule and role assignment · Change records
role_functions.success: Rate of meeting requirements, and deadlines

role_functions.name: Exploration and research
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.output_kind: Research proposal · Preliminary research results · Paper
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed and a method remains

role_functions.name: Writing Standards and Norms
role_functions.one_line: Makes sure standards are kept all the time
role_functions.success: The same errors do not come back, and the basis of decisions can be traced

role_functions_note: There are eight, and they use **the same codes** as the Mechanical Engineering Core. Role functions are a layer above the major, so they are not created again for each major. The names were changed into the words of language and literature majors. The meaning of the work is kept the same, so the axes do not split; what differs is the kind of output: manuscripts, lesson plans and review comments take the place of drawings

org_contexts.name: Publishing and Media Companies
org_contexts.performance: Sales and views · Deadlines · Contract renewal
org_contexts.differs: My manuscript becomes a product right away

org_contexts.name: Contract Translation and Service Companies
org_contexts.performance: Meeting client specifications · Delivery dates · Repeat requests
org_contexts.differs: The guidelines of one client set the standard

org_contexts.name: Education Service Companies
org_contexts.differs: Whether learners come back next month is the evaluation

org_contexts.name: Public Cultural and Language Institutions
org_contexts.performance: Project performance · Interim evaluation · Public value
org_contexts.differs: Work moves by projects, and evaluations set the schedule

org_contexts.name: Universities and Research Institutes
org_contexts.performance: Papers and degrees · Research ethics · Winning research projects
org_contexts.differs: You check on your own whether the method is right and leave it as a paper

org_contexts.name: Assessment and Certification Institutions
org_contexts.performance: Judging whether standards are met · Throughput · Records
org_contexts.differs: The traceability of the judgment is the output

org_contexts.name: Small Studios and Freelance Work
org_contexts.performance: Manuscript fees and the next job
org_contexts.differs: One person takes on planning, writing and editing at the same time

boundaries.a_difference: Collects and sorts which materials to use
boundaries.b_difference: Builds a framework and reads the meaning of those materials
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen the range to search and the materials to use yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you built a reading framework and interpreted with evidence?

boundaries.pair: Language Structure Analysis vs Corpus Data
boundaries.a_difference: Breaks one phenomenon into units and describes it
boundaries.b_difference: Collects a lot of data, processes it, and makes it countable
boundaries.a_question: Have you divided units of sound, form or sentence structure yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set annotation criteria or the data to filter out yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Carries over meaning written in another language
boundaries.b_difference: Revises and publishes text written in this language
boundaries.a_question: Have you chosen the unit of translation and what to keep yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you separated the range to change from the range to keep yourself?

boundaries.pair: Education Design vs Class Management and Assessment
boundaries.a_difference: Decides what to teach and in what order
boundaries.b_difference: Runs that class and judges how much was achieved
boundaries.a_question: Have you set learning goals and the order of units yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set scoring criteria yourself and applied them?

boundaries.shared: Produces something that did not exist
boundaries.a_difference: Builds the story to write and its structure
boundaries.b_difference: Puts together where and in what format to publish
boundaries.a_question: Have you built what to write and its structure yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you chosen the place and format to publish in yourself?

boundaries.pair: Culture and Area Studies vs Research Design
boundaries.a_difference: Reads the existing context and applies it
boundaries.b_difference: Creates new data from people when there is none
boundaries.a_question: Have you changed a judgment based on the context of that region?
boundaries.b_question: Have you decided yourself whom to ask what?

boundaries.shared: Makes the form of a text consistent
boundaries.a_difference: Sets standards for spelling and terms and makes people follow them
boundaries.b_difference: Revises text to make it readable and publishes it
boundaries.a_question: Have you set writing standards or terms yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you revised sentences yourself with the readers in mind?

boundaries.a_difference: Makes the language usable for learners
boundaries.b_difference: Carries over something already written into another language
boundaries.a_question: Have you set the range of vocabulary yourself to fit the learners' level?
boundaries.b_question: When translating, have you separated yourself what to keep and what to drop?

boundaries.a_difference: Decides what to measure and where the line for the correct answer is
boundaries.b_difference: Reads what that text says, based on evidence
boundaries.a_question: Have you decided yourself what an item measures and where the line for the correct answer is?
boundaries.b_question: When the same text could be read in two ways, have you decided based on evidence?

boundaries.a_difference: Creates new data by asking people
boundaries.b_difference: Finds and selects what already exists
boundaries.a_question: Have you decided yourself whom to ask and the order of questions?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set the search words and the materials to filter out yourself?
